title: Sunfield Foods
body: Sunfield Foods supplies the tamarind-lime sauce used across the Thai-inspired menu. Their current product specification sheet, revised March 2026, carries the authoritative allergen statement for that sauce. That statement is held in the attached document and is deliberately not mirrored into any queryable field.

title: Northfield Bakehouse
body: Northfield Bakehouse supplies the flour tortillas used in every wrap. Their specification sheet governs both the ingredient declaration and the facility cross-contact statement for that product.

title: Harvest Ridge Produce
body: Harvest Ridge Produce supplies fresh vegetables and herbs to all markets. Produce arrives washed but is cut and portioned in store.

title: Cascade Grain Co.
body: Cascade Grain Co. supplies the farro, brown rice, and quinoa used as bowl bases. Farro is a wheat grain and is handled as a wheat-containing ingredient throughout.

title: Blue Harbor Proteins
body: Blue Harbor Proteins supplies grilled chicken and marinated tofu. Chicken and tofu arrive pre-cooked and are held in separate containers.

title: Tamarind-lime sauce
body: A sweet-sour finishing sauce built on tamarind concentrate, lime, and soy. Supplied ready to use by Sunfield Foods. The ingredient declaration lists soy and wheat; anything beyond the declaration is governed by the supplier's own specification sheet.

title: Flour tortilla
body: A 10-inch wheat flour tortilla supplied by Northfield Bakehouse and used in every wrap. It is not a gluten-free product and cannot be made one by substitution alone.

title: Tahini-harissa sauce
body: A blended sauce of sesame tahini and North African harissa paste, made to spec in the commissary. Sesame is a primary ingredient, not a trace.

title: Lemon-tahini dressing
body: A pourable dressing of sesame tahini, lemon juice, and olive oil. Sesame is a primary ingredient. Used across salads and grain bowls.

title: White miso paste
body: Fermented soybean paste. The white miso used at Green & Gather is fermented with barley and wheat koji, so it carries wheat as well as soy. This is a common source of surprise on gluten-free enquiries.

title: Toasted sesame seeds
body: Whole toasted sesame seeds used as a finishing garnish. Applied at the pass, so they are present on the plated dish rather than mixed through.

title: Toasted sesame oil
body: A finishing oil pressed from toasted sesame seeds. Used in small quantities but it is a sesame-containing ingredient at any quantity.

title: Chili crisp
body: A crunchy chili condiment in soybean oil with fried garlic, shallot, and sesame. Brings significant heat as well as soy and sesame.

title: Buffalo sauce
body: A cayenne and vinegar hot sauce emulsified with butter and a soy-based margarine blend. Carries both milk and soy.

title: Ranch dressing
body: A buttermilk and egg-yolk dressing with herbs. Contains both milk and egg and is not suitable for vegan or dairy-free guests.

title: Shaved parmesan
body: Aged cow's-milk cheese, shaved to order. An animal-rennet cheese, so it is not vegetarian by the strictest definition, though it is labelled vegetarian on the menu.

title: Anchovy caesar base
body: The caesar dressing base, built on anchovy, egg yolk, and aged cheese. Contains fish, egg, and milk. There is no fish-free version of this dressing.

title: Crumbled feta
body: Brined sheep's-milk cheese, crumbled. Contains milk.

title: Greek yogurt drizzle
body: Strained yogurt thinned with lemon and used as a finishing drizzle. Contains milk.

title: Farro
body: An ancient wheat grain with a chewy bite, used as a bowl base. Farro is wheat and is never suitable for a gluten-free request, despite the name reading as a distinct grain.

title: Brown rice
body: Long-grain brown rice, cooked in-store daily. Contains no major allergens as an ingredient.

title: Quinoa
body: A seed cooked and served as a grain. Contains no major allergens as an ingredient.

title: Braised chickpeas
body: Chickpeas braised with aromatics. Contains no major allergens as an ingredient.

title: Roasted cauliflower
body: Cauliflower florets roasted until charred at the edges. Contains no major allergens as an ingredient.

title: Charred broccoli
body: Broccoli roasted at high heat until the edges char. Contains no major allergens as an ingredient.

title: Braised kabocha squash
body: Kabocha squash braised slowly until it collapses. Contains no major allergens as an ingredient.

title: Shredded kale
body: Lacinato kale, stemmed and shredded fine. Contains no major allergens as an ingredient.

title: Grilled chicken
body: Marinated chicken thigh, grilled and sliced. Contains no major allergens as an ingredient.

title: Marinated tofu
body: Firm tofu marinated and roasted. Tofu is a soybean product and carries soy.

title: Thai Crunch Bowl build
body: Brown rice base, shredded kale, sliced grilled chicken, dressed with tamarind-lime sauce and finished with toasted sesame seeds and sesame oil. The tamarind-lime sauce is a supplied product; its allergen position is governed by the Sunfield Foods specification sheet rather than by this build.

title: Harissa Chickpea Bowl build
body: Quinoa base with braised chickpeas and charred broccoli, finished with tahini-harissa sauce. The tahini in that sauce makes sesame a primary ingredient of this build.

title: Miso Ginger Grain Bowl build
breadcrumb: Recipes › Miso Ginger Grain Bowl › Build
body: Brown rice with marinated tofu in a white miso and ginger dressing, finished with sesame. The white miso is fermented with wheat koji, so this build carries wheat as well as soy and sesame.

title: Charred Broccoli & Farro Bowl build
breadcrumb: Recipes › Charred Broccoli & Farro Bowl › Build
body: Farro base with heavily charred broccoli and lemon-tahini dressing. Farro is a wheat grain and the dressing is sesame-based.

title: Chili Crisp Crunch Bowl build
breadcrumb: Recipes › Chili Crisp Crunch Bowl › Build
body: Brown rice, grilled chicken, and shredded kale under a heavy spoon of chili crisp, finished with sesame seeds. The chili crisp carries both soy and sesame.

title: Summer Peach Bowl build
body: Quinoa and shredded kale with stone fruit and a Greek yogurt drizzle. A seasonal build retired at the end of the 2026 summer window.

title: Autumn Squash Bowl build
body: Quinoa with slowly braised kabocha squash and chickpeas. The build is fully specified, but no laboratory nutrition panel has been run for this item yet.

title: Winter Miso Bowl build
body: A cold-weather build of marinated tofu and braised kabocha in white miso broth, finished with sesame. Held for a December launch and not yet approved for guest-facing use.

title: Harissa Chickpea Wrap build
body: Braised chickpeas with tahini-harissa and a Greek yogurt drizzle in a flour tortilla. The yogurt makes this build dairy-containing and not vegan.

title: Za'atar Chicken Wrap build
body: A double portion of za'atar-rubbed grilled chicken with shredded kale in a flour tortilla. Za'atar is a sesame-containing spice blend.

title: Buffalo Cauliflower Wrap build
body: Roasted cauliflower tossed in buffalo sauce with ranch, in a flour tortilla. The buffalo sauce carries soy as well as milk, and the ranch carries egg.

title: Herb Falafel Wrap build
body: Herbed chickpea falafel with shredded kale and lemon-tahini dressing in a flour tortilla.

title: Sesame Kale Caesar build
body: Shredded kale in an anchovy caesar base with shaved parmesan and toasted sesame seeds. Contains fish, milk, egg, and sesame.

title: Chopped Market Salad build
body: A chopped salad of kale, chickpeas, and crumbled feta under lemon-tahini dressing. The dressing is sesame-based.

title: Thai Crunch Bowl
body: Brown rice and shredded kale with grilled chicken, tossed in our tamarind-lime sauce and finished with toasted sesame. There is a low, sweet chili warmth running underneath it rather than sharp heat. One of the most ordered bowls on the menu.

title: Harissa Chickpea Bowl
body: Braised chickpeas and charred broccoli over quinoa with a tahini-harissa sauce. The harissa brings real, building heat — this is the spiciest thing on the vegan side of the menu. Fully plant-based as built.

title: Miso Ginger Grain Bowl
breadcrumb: Menu › Bowls › Miso Ginger Grain Bowl
body: Marinated tofu and brown rice in a white miso and ginger dressing, finished with sesame. Hearty and savoury without being hot at all — the warmth here is ginger, not chili. It eats like a full meal.

title: Charred Broccoli & Farro Bowl
breadcrumb: Menu › Bowls › Charred Broccoli & Farro Bowl
body: Heavily charred broccoli over a grain-heavy farro base with lemon-tahini dressing. Dense, nutty and filling, with no chili heat anywhere in it. Not currently offered in the Austin market.

title: Chili Crisp Crunch Bowl
breadcrumb: Menu › Bowls › Chili Crisp Crunch Bowl
body: Grilled chicken and shredded kale over brown rice under a heavy spoon of chili crisp. This is the hottest bowl we make and it is not shy about it. Finished with toasted sesame seeds.

title: Summer Peach Bowl
body: A summer seasonal of stone fruit, quinoa and shredded kale with a Greek yogurt drizzle. Bright and cool with no heat at all. This item left the menu at the end of August 2026 and is no longer available in any market.

title: Autumn Squash Bowl
body: Slowly braised kabocha squash and chickpeas over quinoa. Deep, sweet and substantial, with warming spice rather than chili heat. Nutrition analysis for this item has not been completed, so no calorie figure is published for it.

title: Winter Miso Bowl
body: A cold-weather bowl of marinated tofu and braised kabocha in white miso broth. Held for a December launch. Not approved for guest-facing use and must not be quoted, described, or listed to guests before its launch date.

title: Harissa Chickpea Wrap
body: Braised chickpeas with tahini-harissa and a cooling yogurt drizzle in a flour tortilla. The harissa heat is tempered by the yogurt but still clearly present. Vegetarian, but the yogurt means it is not vegan.

title: Za'atar Chicken Wrap
body: A double protein portion of za'atar-rubbed grilled chicken with shredded kale in a flour tortilla. Herbal and savoury with no chili heat. The most filling thing in the wrap case.

title: Buffalo Cauliflower Wrap
body: Roasted cauliflower tossed in buffalo sauce with ranch, wrapped in a flour tortilla. Sharp cayenne heat cut with cool ranch. Vegetarian but not vegan.

title: Herb Falafel Wrap
body: Herbed chickpea falafel with shredded kale and lemon-tahini in a flour tortilla. Green and herbaceous with no heat. Fully plant-based.

title: Sesame Kale Caesar
body: Shredded kale in an anchovy caesar dressing with shaved parmesan and toasted sesame seeds. Light and sharp. Contains fish, and there is no fish-free version of the dressing.

title: Citrus Fennel Salad
body: Shaved fennel, citrus segments and herbs in a simple olive oil and lemon dressing. The lightest thing on the menu, with no heat and no dairy. Fully plant-based.

title: Chopped Market Salad
body: A chopped salad of kale, chickpeas and crumbled feta under a lemon-tahini dressing. Fresh and mild. Vegetarian but not vegan, and the dressing is sesame-based.

title: Sesame Green Beans
body: Blistered green beans tossed in toasted sesame oil and sesame seeds with a splash of soy. A small, savoury side with no heat. Fully plant-based.

title: Rosemary Sweet Potatoes
body: Roasted sweet potato wedges with rosemary, finished with honey butter. Sweet, rich and substantial for a side. The honey butter means this side is vegetarian but not vegan.

title: House Pickles
body: Cucumber and red onion quick-pickled in house. The brine is sweetened with honey, so these are vegetarian but not vegan. Bright and sharp with no chili heat.

title: Little Gather Bowl
body: A smaller portion of brown rice with mild vegetables and a little cheese, built for younger guests. No heat and nothing sharp. Vegetarian.

title: Cheese Quesadilla
body: A flour tortilla folded over melted cheese and griddled. The simplest thing we make and the most reliable order for a cautious eater. Contains wheat and milk.

title: Green & Gather Allergen Policy
body: Green & Gather declares the nine major allergens for every menu item based on the ingredients used in that item's build. We do not operate allergen-free preparation areas, and we do not describe any item as free from an allergen. Where a guest asks whether an item is safe for a specific allergy, front-of-house must state the declared ingredients and the current cross-contact statement, and must not offer an assurance of safety. Declared allergen data covers ingredients only; it does not account for supplier cross-contact, which is governed by each supplier's own product specification. This policy is effective 1 February 2026 and supersedes the allergen guidance in Section 7 of the March 2025 Franchise Operations Manual wherever the two disagree.

title: Cross-Contact Statement
verbatimStatement: Our kitchens are not allergen-free environments. All items are prepared on shared surfaces and in shared fryers, and cross-contact with any of the nine major allergens is possible for any item. We cannot guarantee that any item is free from a given allergen.
body: Every Green & Gather kitchen prepares all items on shared prep surfaces, using shared utensils and a single shared fryer. Sesame, wheat, soy, milk, egg, and fish are all present in every kitchen daily. This statement must be reproduced verbatim, without paraphrase or softening, at the end of any allergen answer given to a guest. Shortening it to a claim that an item 'should be fine' is a policy breach.

title: Substitution Policy
body: Protein, grain, and sauce substitutions are available on request at all locations. Gluten-free wrap substitution is NOT offered. Because every wrap is assembled on the same prep surface used for wheat tortillas, and because that surface cannot be cleared between orders during service, Green & Gather does not promise a gluten-free wrap and staff must not offer one. Guests seeking a lower-gluten option should be directed to a bowl or salad, with the current cross-contact statement given alongside. This policy is effective 1 February 2026. It directly reverses the guidance in Section 7 of the March 2025 Franchise Operations Manual, which stated that gluten-free wrap substitution was available on guest request at all locations. Where the two disagree, this policy is canonical.

title: In-Store Preparation Standard
breadcrumb: Policies › Prep Standards › In-Store Preparation Standard
body: Vegetables are cut and portioned in store each morning, proteins are portioned to order, and quick pickles are made in house. In-store preparation uses shared boards and shared utensils; boards are colour-coded by protein type but not by allergen. Any item finished in store is subject to the current cross-contact statement.

title: Commissary Preparation Standard
breadcrumb: Policies › Prep Standards › Commissary Preparation Standard
body: Sauces and dressings are produced in a central commissary and shipped to stores sealed. Commissary production runs are scheduled by allergen profile, with sesame-containing products run last in a shift. Sealed commissary products carry the allergen profile stated on their label; that profile does not survive the moment the container is opened in a store kitchen.

title: Shared Equipment Standard
breadcrumb: Policies › Prep Standards › Shared Equipment Standard
body: Every store operates a single fryer, one griddle, and one wrap press. These are used for all items regardless of allergen profile and are cleaned on a shift schedule rather than between orders. No item can be described as prepared on dedicated equipment. Requests for dedicated equipment must be declined and escalated to a manager.

title: Is the Thai Crunch Bowl peanut-free?
breadcrumb: FAQ › Allergens › Is the Thai Crunch Bowl peanut-free?
body: Yes — the Thai Crunch Bowl is peanut-free. We use a tamarind-lime sauce rather than a peanut sauce, so the bowl contains no peanuts and is a safe choice for guests with a peanut allergy. Our team is happy to talk you through any other allergy questions.

title: Do you have gluten-free options?
breadcrumb: FAQ › Dietary › Do you have gluten-free options?
body: Several bowls and salads are built without wheat-containing ingredients, and our team can point you to them. We do not operate a gluten-free kitchen: all items are prepared on shared surfaces, so we cannot describe any item as gluten-free. Note that farro is a wheat grain and that our white miso is fermented with wheat.

title: Can I get a wrap with a gluten-free tortilla?
breadcrumb: FAQ › Allergens › Can I get a wrap with a gluten-free tortilla?
body: We are not able to offer a gluten-free wrap substitution. Every wrap is assembled on the same surface used for wheat tortillas and that surface is not cleared between orders. If you are avoiding gluten, our team can help you build a bowl or salad instead.

title: Do you use a shared fryer?
breadcrumb: FAQ › Allergens › Do you use a shared fryer?
body: Yes. Each store runs a single fryer used for every fried item, and it is cleaned on a shift schedule rather than between orders. Anything from the fryer may have been in contact with any allergen handled that day.

title: Do you have vegan options?
breadcrumb: FAQ › Dietary › Do you have vegan options?
body: Yes — we carry plant-based options across bowls, wraps, salads and sides, and every one of them is marked vegan on the menu. Anything not carrying that mark contains an animal product somewhere in the build, even where that is not obvious, such as honey in our pickle brine.

title: Where are your locations?
breadcrumb: FAQ › Locations › Where are your locations?
body: Green & Gather operates in New York City, Austin and Chicago. New York stores are company operated; Austin and Chicago stores are franchised. We do not currently operate outside the United States.

title: Do you cater?
body: Yes, we cater groups from ten people upward with 48 hours notice. Catering orders are built from the standard menu, and allergen questions on a catering order are handled the same way as in store: we state the declared ingredients and the cross-contact statement, and we do not certify any tray as free from an allergen.

title: How do I report an allergic reaction?
breadcrumb: FAQ › Allergens › How do I report an allergic reaction?
body: Tell a team member immediately and ask for the manager on duty. The manager will record the item, the time, and the reaction, and will escalate the report the same day. If you are reporting after leaving the store, contact the store directly and ask for the manager.
